name: Nutrition
goal: Regular meal times, enough water, plenty of plants and a protein-rich breakfast.

rules.title: Breakfast at the usual time
rules.label: Breakfast
rules.why: A regular meal pattern improves insulin sensitivity and thermogenesis compared with an irregular one; meal timing entrains peripheral body clocks.
rules.advice: Have breakfast at your usual time.

nudge.text: Breakfast in 15 minutes — same time as usual keeps your metabolic clock in sync.

pairs.text: Make it protein-rich: eggs, yogurt or cottage cheese.

rules.title: Lunch at the usual time
rules.label: Lunch
rules.why: Irregular meal timing is associated with worse cardiometabolic markers; regular timing lets the body anticipate food.
rules.advice: Block lunch at your usual time.

nudge.text: Lunch in 15 minutes. Wrap up and keep the slot.

pairs.text: Fill half the plate with vegetables.

rules.title: Dinner at the usual time
rules.label: Dinner
rules.why: Consistent meal times are part of the AHA recommendation for intentional meal timing.
rules.advice: Have dinner at your usual time.

nudge.text: Dinner in 15 minutes — at the usual time.

pairs.text: Fill half the plate with vegetables.

rules.title: No food within 3 h of bed
rules.label: Kitchen closed
rules.why: Late eating impairs glucose tolerance and fat oxidation compared with an earlier meal.
rules.advice: Kitchen is closed — water or herbal tea only.

rules.title: Water after waking
rules.label: Water on waking
rules.why: You lose water overnight; even mild dehydration lowers mood and concentration.
rules.advice: A full glass of water before coffee.

nudge.text: Glass of water before coffee — you lose water overnight.

rules.title: Water through the afternoon
rules.label: Afternoon water
rules.why: The afternoon dip is partly thirst: mild dehydration impairs attention and raises perceived effort.

nudge.text: Afternoon check: a glass of water now beats another coffee.

rules.title: Vegetables with lunch
rules.label: Veg with lunch
rules.why: Each extra daily portion of fruit and vegetables lowers cardiovascular and all-cause mortality, up to ~800 g a day.

rules.title: Vegetables with dinner
rules.label: Veg with dinner
rules.why: Each extra daily portion of fruit and vegetables lowers cardiovascular and all-cause mortality, up to ~800 g a day.

rules.title: Protein at breakfast
rules.label: Protein breakfast
rules.why: A higher-protein breakfast improves satiety signals and reduces evening snacking compared with a low-protein one.
rules.advice: Eggs, yogurt, cottage cheese or tofu.
